questions.prompt: Calculate \(\mathcal L\{e^{1t}t\}(s)\) using the exponential-shift property.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
Since \(\mathcal L\{t\}(s)=1/s^2\), replace \(s\) by \(s-1\):
\[\mathcal L\{e^{1t}t\}=\frac1{(s-1)^2}.\]
Final answer: \(1/(s-1)^2\), for \(s>1\).

questions.prompt:
Part (a): Calculate \(\mathcal L\{e^{13t}t\}(s)\) using the exponential-shift property.
Part (b): Derive the derivative property \(\mathcal L\{f'\}=sF(s)-f(0)\).
questions.answer:
Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
Since \(\mathcal L\{t\}(s)=1/s^2\), replace \(s\) by \(s-13\):
\[\mathcal L\{e^{13t}t\}=\frac1{(s-13)^2}.\]
Final answer: \(1/(s-13)^2\), for \(s>13\).

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
Integration by parts gives
\[\int_0^\infty e^{-st}f'(t)dt=[e^{-st}f(t)]_0^\infty+s\int_0^\infty e^{-st}f(t)dt=-f(0)+sF(s).\]
Final answer: \(\mathcal L\{f'\}=sF-f(0)\).
